Synopsis:
The bandits are encountered near an abandoned chapel and are in the middle of an argument among themselves about whether or not to investigate (and loot) the crashed nautoloid (a spaceship) when the player approaches them. The player can convince them to clear off via lies or threats, or else is forced to fight them. A gnome named Gimblebock is in charge of this group, with his underlings, Quelanna and/or Taman, chiming in at points with their concerns.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_Outside_BanditInteraction.json: You approach a small band of scrappy bandits — led by the gnome Gimblebock with underlings like Taman (and sometimes Quelanna) — who have been squabbling outside an abandoned chapel/tomb about whether to investigate and loot the crashed nautiloid nearby. Off‑screen the group has already noted the crypt beneath the chapel (other bandits, Mari and Barton, have been trying to break in), and the party has interrupted their argument. The scene is set before a worn bronze plaque at the base of a statue inside the tomb; the inscription is illegible to you and your companions (no scholar or translation magic is available), so any player claims about the plaque or the ship are speculative. Gimblebock blusters bravely but can be cowed by threats or lies, which can make the bandits stand down — otherwise the exchange can escalate into a fight.
- CHA_Outside_BanditBackInteraction_Spotted.json: You’ve just emerged from an old, neglected chapel/tomb of Selûne where you and your party reached a small sanctum with a worn statue and an unreadable bronze plaque — the group currently lacks a reliable way to translate the inscription. Outside the ruin a small gang of bandits, led by Gimblebock, argue among themselves; they thought the crypt was theirs, have people posted inside, and are suddenly alarmed to see you coming out. They’re worried about the fate of their friend left in the chapel and shift quickly between bluster and panic, accusing you of poaching their loot or attacking outright. Depending on how you respond (threats, demands, or violence) they may back down and flee or escalate into a fight.
- UND_DeadInTheWater_CorpseDisposers.json: Two grouchy duergar, one a talker and one who somewhat mimics/ repeats what his partner says, are responsible for dumping dead gnome bodies into the lake. You can convince them to let you loot the bodies.
- FOR_ApothecaryGoblins_Goblin_02.json: This goblin is leading a band of looters in an abandoned house. They're too distracted by greed to fight, but if the player persists they'll attack.
- CHA_Outside_BanditWestInteraction.json: You’re in a dusty tomb-chapel before a statue with a worn bronze plaque whose inscription is illegible to the party (no scholar or translation has been provided), so any guesses about cults or gods are speculative. Approaching from the side alerted Warryn, who yells up to his boss Gimblebock (who was down some steps), so the bandits scramble to confront you rather than being surprised. Gimblebock is the gang’s leader and was in the middle of claiming/looting the crypt or the nearby crashed ship; he alternates between bluster and real nervousness when the player warns or threatens them. His underling Taman nervously corrects his mixed metaphor while Gimblebock tries to reassert control and orders the others to move.
